title: Vatican Archives - The Room With No Windows

target.note: short declaratives, one idea per beat. Little to no pause between sentences.

narration:
Beneath Vatican City there is an archive.
The rooms down there have no windows.
The place is called the Vatican Archives.
The archive doors opened in 1939.
They opened once, for outside scholars.
Then the doors closed again, quietly.
The rooms run deep under the hill.
The shelves stretch out for kilometres.
A wooden ladder slides along a rail.
No electric light is allowed down there.
Every window was walled up on purpose.
Nobody may photograph a single page.
Not even a phone screen is allowed.
A camera flash would harm the paper.
Some of that paper cannot be opened.
The old pages have fused together.
Open them and the paper tears.
So most of those boxes stay shut.
Some documents are never consulted again.
They were catalogued once, then shelved.
A single index card, one line on it.
That one line is the whole record.
Fragile pages are filmed instead of opened.
Other pages stay closed for ever.
A microfilm reel beside a sealed box.
The shelving system itself is kept quiet.
Few people know how the stacks run.
The actual plan is filed elsewhere, upstairs.
Nobody has ever carried it down.
A reader lost between two tall shelves.
The Vatican has shelved many older records.
Some have stayed shut for years.
Others open for a chosen few only.
Access is a favour, not a right.
A hand holding out a small key.
The stacks hold centuries nobody has read.
Nobody knows what is on the lowest shelves.
The dark down there is absolute.

beats.line: Beneath Vatican City there is an archive.
beats.visual: cross-section of a hill under Vatican City, one dark chamber cut into the rock, filling the frame

beats.line: The rooms down there have no windows.
beats.visual: close on a windowless stone wall, bricks filled in where glass would be

beats.line: The place is called the Vatican Archives.
beats.visual: hand-lettered 'THE VATICAN ARCHIVES' stamped tall across the archive door

beats.line: The archive doors opened in 1939.
beats.visual: old calendar page with the year 1939 ringed in red pencil

beats.line: They opened once, for outside scholars.
beats.visual: a small group of scholars at a plain wooden table, no ornament

beats.line: Then the doors closed again, quietly.
beats.visual: the same heavy door shut again, character standing deadpan before it

beats.line: The rooms run deep under the hill.
beats.visual: cutaway of stacked chambers descending under the hill, each one deeper than the last

beats.line: The shelves stretch out for kilometres.
beats.visual: one endless shelf run filling the frame edge to edge, receding to no end

beats.line: A wooden ladder slides along a rail.
beats.visual: wooden rolling ladder hooked onto a shelf rail, close

beats.line: No electric light is allowed down there.
beats.visual: bare bulb behind a wire cage, switched off; label 'NO ELECTRIC LIGHT'

beats.line: Every window was walled up on purpose.
beats.visual: mason's blocked-up window arch, fresh brick inside an old stone frame

beats.line: Nobody may photograph a single page.
beats.visual: a hand holding a camera below a page, red slash across it; character shrugging

beats.line: Not even a phone screen is allowed.
beats.visual: phone screen glowing flat on a cradle beside a parchment sheet

beats.line: A camera flash would harm the paper.
beats.visual: camera flash burst drawn as a white star over brittle brown paper

beats.line: Some of that paper cannot be opened.
beats.visual: an open box of fused pages, edges welded in a single pale block

beats.line: The old pages have fused together.
beats.visual: close on two pages stuck face to face, a torn corner hanging loose

beats.line: Open them and the paper tears.
beats.visual: a page being lifted and splitting, jagged tear line in red

beats.line: So most of those boxes stay shut.
beats.visual: lid lowered on a wooden box, hands flat on the shut top

beats.line: Some documents are never consulted again.
beats.visual: character reaching for a box, then stopping; speech bubble 'not this one'

beats.line: They were catalogued once, then shelved.
beats.visual: an old catalogue page with one single line of handwriting, the rest blank

beats.line: A single index card, one line on it.
beats.visual: one index card in a card tray, most of the tray empty around it

beats.line: That one line is the whole record.
beats.visual: magnifier over that one line of writing, character awed

beats.line: Fragile pages are filmed instead of opened.
beats.visual: a reel-to-reel microfilm machine, a page flattened under the lens

beats.line: Other pages stay closed for ever.
beats.visual: a sealed box on a shelf stamped with a red 'CLOSED' band

beats.line: A microfilm reel beside a sealed box.
beats.visual: microfilm reel on the left, sealed box on the right, drawn to the same size

beats.line: The shelving system itself is kept quiet.
beats.visual: a diagram of the whole stack layout, half covered by a hand

beats.line: Few people know how the stacks run.
beats.visual: character squinting at a shelf-end placard, shoulders hunched

beats.line: The actual plan is filed elsewhere, upstairs.
beats.visual: a plan rolled up and locked in an upstairs drawer, labelled in a different hand

beats.line: Nobody has ever carried it down.
beats.visual: an empty hand leaving the stairs, no plan in it; floor line drawn as a threshold

beats.line: A reader lost between two tall shelves.
beats.visual: character small, seen from above, wedged between two towering shelf faces

beats.line: The Vatican has shelved many older records.
beats.visual: shelf row with a wide dark gap where bound volumes should sit

beats.line: Some have stayed shut for years.
beats.visual: a wall calendar with a decade of pages unturned, thick and swollen

beats.line: Others open for a chosen few only.
beats.visual: one box drawn out on a table under a lamp, three people standing at a respectful distance

beats.line: Access is a favour, not a right.
beats.visual: a hand held out flat, palm up; character looking away from it

beats.line: A hand holding out a small key.
beats.visual: one small key resting in an open palm, flat fills, plain background

beats.line: The stacks hold centuries nobody has read.
beats.visual: vast shelf run again, this time packed with unlabelled boxes, none of them open

beats.line: Nobody knows what is on the lowest shelves.
beats.visual: character at the bottom of a shelf, looking down; speech bubble 'nobody knows'

beats.line: The dark down there is absolute.
beats.visual: the lowest shelf in near-total black, only the character awed at the edge of the dark
